title: Gold plummets ₹15,200/10g as dollar strength peaks at ₹96.21 exchange rate
summary: MCX gold crashed ₹15,200 per 10 grams today amid a firm US dollar, with spot rates now trading near ₹161,571/10g. Silver suffered steeper losses of ₹72,000 per kilogram, reflecting intense dollar-buying pressure that weakens precious metals priced in rupees. For Indian traders, elevated import costs on gold jewelry and investment demand face headwinds as rupee depreciation increases duty calculations and working capital requirements. The sharp correction presents tactical opportunities for physical demand in the domestic market. Watch for RBI policy signals and US inflation data release this week—a softer dollar narrative could trigger sharp reversals in both contracts.

Watch for global gold support at $4,500/oz and domestic import duty announcements affecting fabricator procurement strategies.
